details:
Q1: How should the dependency phase's network access be restricted?
Choices:
A. Run the dependency container with `--network none` as well. Add an allowlisting HTTPS proxy on the host, built the same way as the model broker in `scripts/clarify_openrouter_broker.py` (host broker on a Unix socket plus an in-container loopback bridge). It only lets connections through to package-registry hosts. pip and npm reach it through `HTTPS_PROXY`. It stays one install phase: build backends can still reach the public registries but nothing internal. (RECOMMENDED)
B. Same proxy as A, plus a split into two phases: first a proxied download of wheels only (`pip download --only-binary=:all:`, `npm ci --ignore-scripts`), then the editable install and any builds with `--no-index` and no proxy at all. This is stricter, but more consumer packages that only ship source distributions will fail to install. Those failures don't stop the run; the agent marks the affected checks UNVERIFIED.
C. No proxy. Download wheels only on the normal Docker network, then build and install offline with `--network none`. pip and npm themselves can still fetch any URL a lockfile or requirements file names, but they can't run attacker code.
Q2: Which hosts should the dependency phase be allowed to reach? (Only relevant if Q1 is A or B.)
Choices:
A. A fixed default list (`pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `registry.npmjs.org`, `registry.yarnpkg.com`). A new repo variable with that list as its default lets a repo add public mirrors such as `download.pytorch.org`. Any requirements or lockfile URL on another host is refused and logged. (RECOMMENDED)
B. The fixed default list only, with no way to extend it. Repos that use `--extra-index-url` mirrors will lose those dependencies, and the agent will mark the affected checks UNVERIFIED.
